title: The Gannon storm, 10 to 11 May 2024

kp.meaning: Planetary Kp for the 3-hour interval that starts at t0_unix + i * step_s (0 to 9, in thirds: 4.667 = 5-).

solar_wind.meaning: 5-minute means of 1-minute OMNI data, time-shifted from the L1 spacecraft to Earth's bow shock nose (so the times are when the wind reached Earth, about 30 to 60 minutes after L1). Bz is the north-south field in GSM coordinates (negative = southward, which couples to Earth's field); Bt is the field strength. null = no measurement.

xray.meaning: GOES XRS X-ray flux at Earth in W/m^2. long = 0.1-0.8 nm (XRS-B, the channel that sets the flare class: A < 1e-7 <= B < 1e-6 <= C < 1e-5 <= M < 1e-4 <= X). short = 0.05-0.4 nm (XRS-A). Each value is the highest 1-minute value in its 5 minutes, so flare peaks are kept. null = no good measurement (for example when the satellite was in Earth's shadow around the equinoxes).

aurora.ovation_note: NOAA SWPC does not archive its OVATION Prime aurora forecasts, so past events use the Kp-driven oval model.

notes: The storm is named after Jennifer Gannon, a space weather scientist who died shortly before it.
The first G5 (extreme) geomagnetic storm since October 2003. Several CMEs from sunspot group AR 13664, launched on 8 and 9 May, arrived together from 16:36 UT on 10 May.
